{{Quote|Governor Tarkin, we're curious to know how you knew you were being deceived at your base of operations.|Sate Pestage|<ref name="Tarkin" />}}
'''Sate Pestage''' was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] official who served on the [[Imperial Ruling Council|Ruling Council]] of the [[Galactic Empire]].<ref name="Tarkin" /> During the [[Clone Wars]], he served as a [[Senior Advisor]] of [[Supreme Chancellor]] [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine]] who sometimes acted as a [[bureaucrat]], [[emissary]], or a dignitary in Palpatine's name<ref name="RotS">''[[Rise of the Separatists]]''</ref> and one time accompanied [[Janus Greejatus]], [[Ars Dangor]], [[Sly Moore]] and [[Lieutenant Commander]] [[Orson Callan Krennic|Orson Krennic]] to [[Geonosis]] to oversee [[Poggle the Lesser]]'s homecoming. As Poggle gave a speech to his fellow [[Geonosian]]s, Pestage sat alongside the other emissaries in the [[Petranaki Arena]].<ref name="Catalyst" />

After the [[Proclamation of the New Order|rise]] of the [[Galactic Empire]], Pestage continued to serve [[Galactic Emperor|Emperor]] Palpatine as an [[Emperor's adviser|adviser]]. He had a [[Hair|shaved]] head, pointed chin beard, and raking [[eye]]brows. Like all the other members of the Imperial Ruling Council, he donned [[color]]ful [[robe]]s and floppy [[hat]]s.<ref name="Tarkin" /> In [[14 BBY]],<ref name="Tarkin date">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of [[Tarkin (novel)|''Tarkin'']] to [[14 BBY]].</ref> he attended a meeting of the Ruling Council and [[Joint Chiefs of the Imperial Military|Joint Chiefs]], which also included the Emperor, [[Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]], [[Wilhuff Tarkin]], and [[Grand Vizier]] [[Mas Amedda]]. When Pestage raised the matter of Tarkin's [[Attack on Sentinel Base|encounter]] with the insurgents at [[Sentinel Base]], [[Dodd Rancit]] of the [[Naval Intelligence Agency]] vouched for Tarkin's role in frustrating [[Confederacy of Independent Systems|Separatist]] [[Shadowfeed|propaganda efforts]] during the Clone Wars.<ref name="Tarkin" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|The Emperor will be with you in time.|Sate Pestage, in a cut scene from ''The Empire Strikes Back''|<ref name="Empire 4th Draft">{{WebCite|url=https://www.starwarz.com/starkiller/the-empire-strikes-back-shooting-scriptfourth-draft|text=The Empire Strikes Back – Shooting Script/Fourth Draft|archivedate=20211017150332}}</ref>}}
Sate Pestage was introduced to the new ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]] in [[James Luceno]]'s [[2014]] novel [[Tarkin (novel)|''Tarkin'']].<ref name="Tarkin" /> [[Sate Pestage/Legends|He]] was first introduced in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, first being mentioned in ''[[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back - Official Collectors Edition]]''<ref name="collector">''[[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back - Official Collectors Edition]]''</ref> and first appearing in the [[X-Wing Rogue Squadron 21|21st issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars: X-Wing Rogue Squadron]]'' [[Star Wars comic books|comic book]] series by [[Michael A. Stackpole]].<ref name="X-WRS21">[[X-Wing Rogue Squadron 21|''X-Wing Rogue Squadron'' 21]]</ref> Within Legends he held the position of [[Grand Vizier/Legends|Grand Vizier]],<ref name="warlords">{{SW|url=news/the-imperial-warlords-despoilers-of-an-empire-part-3|series=The Imperial Warlords: Despoilers of an Empire|text=Part 3|nolive=1}}</ref> a [[Grand Vizier|position]] held in canon by [[Mas Amedda]].<ref name="Tarkin" />

Sate Pestage, originally called Sate Molock, was initially meant to appear in the [[1980]] film [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']]. Molock first appeared in the second screenplay draft, where he warns Darth Vader that the Emperor is in a bad mood before Vader reports the Imperial victory over Hoth. In the revised second draft, Molock was renamed Sate Pestage.<ref name="SW:TAS">''[[Star Wars: The Annotated Screenplays]]''</ref>

In Episode V's fourth draft, Pestage was planned to appear in scene 286 as a "shimmering [[Hologram|holographic]] image." When Darth Vader attempts to contact the Emperor, he reaches Pestage, who, as previously mentioned, warns Vader of the Emperor's foul mood and bids him to wait.<ref name="SW:TAS" /> According to [[Lucasfilm Story Group]]'s [[Pablo Hidalgo]], by the fifth script draft of the film, Pestage had been already cut.<ref name="SWI89">{{InsiderCite|89|Ask Lobot|Ask the Master}}</ref>

In [[2003]], a production photo from five of the Advisors seen in the [[1983]] film [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']], the last installment of the ''Star Wars'' [[original trilogy]], was included in [https://web.archive.org/web/20031008010828/www.starwars.com/community/askjc/jocasta/askjc20030602.html an article] published on [[StarWars.com]], accompanied by text that read "Among the members of Palpatine's Inner Circle are: Sate Pestage, [[Janus Greejatus]], [[Sim Aloo]], [[Ars Dangor]], and [[Kren Blista-Vanee]]."<ref name="Ars in RotJ?">{{SWArchive|url=community/askjc/jocasta/askjc20030602.html|text=Ask the Lucasfilm Jedi Council: Who are the gentlemen with the Emperor?}}</ref> In [[September]] [[2023]], after the release of his short story "[[Kernels and Husks]]" in ''[[From a Certain Point of View: Return of the Jedi]]'', author [[Jason Fry]] confirmed that Pestage was the advisor in black robes, canonizing his appearance in the film.<ref name="Twitter">{{Twitter|jasoncfry|status/1697627240442532052|[[Jason Fry]]|date=2023-09-01|quote=That's correct! {{C|In response to: "@jasoncfry Hulloh! :) Could you possibly tell us which one you meant to be Pestage (and therefore which one you meant to be Xorn)? My assumption is Pestage is on the left."}}|archivefile=File:Pestage Twitter.png}}</ref>
